title: Hearthline request: pricing match and transition credits
text:
Hearthline request: pricing match and transition credits

['From: Sara Hunter <sara.hunter@hearthline.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: can Redwood match Streamline pricing?

Hi Sean,

Quick note — we just received a formal replacement offer from Streamline AI for our inference needs. Their proposal is materially lower on per-token pricing for the next 12 months and includes a $75k onboarding credit. Our procurement team asked whether Redwood can match the economics (or provide an alternative bridge) to avoid a migration.

Attached is the Streamline term sheet they sent this morning (Streamline_offer_v2.pdf) and a recent usage snapshot. Can you let me know what flexibility you have and what tradeoffs (term, quantization, throughput) would look like? We’re looking to decide by next week.

Thanks,
Sara Hunter
Head of Platform Engineering
Hearthline Analytics

---
Attachment: Streamline_offer_v2.pdf (application/pdf)', 'From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Sara Hunter <sara.hunter@hearthline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: can Redwood match Streamline pricing?

Sara — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the term sheet. I’ve looped in Marissa (your AE) and Karthik (solutions) so we can evaluate the ask quickly. A few clarifying items that will help us propose a defensible counter:

- Current average monthly token consumption and peak 95th percentile (the snapshot helps but if you have 30/60/90 day bins that’d be ideal)
- Which model profiles (long-form generation vs short chat) are driving the spend
- Whether Hearthline has an existing requirement for private deployment or dedicated capacity (this affects discounting)

We’ll aim to get a preliminary counter by EOD Friday. If it helps, I can also propose short-term credits + a 12-month committed pricing ladder to close the gap without sacrificing latency SLAs.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: hearthline_usage_snapshot.csv (text/csv)', 'From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: internal: Hearthline competitive analysis + proposed counter

Internal — quick read of Streamline terms vs our typical packaging. Key delta: Streamline is offering a ~22% lower unit price for the first 12 months plus a $75k onboarding credit. They’re asking for a 12-month minimum commitment.

Proposed counter (high level):
- 12-month committed tier with stepping discounts: 0–5B tokens @ baseline, 5–20B @ -15%, 20B+ @ -22% (matches at scale)
- $50k onboarding credit applied as first-invoice credit / professional services credit
- 60-day technical migration support (engineer hours) to reduce switching risk
- Optional 6-month price protection for sustained usage above baseline

Risks/notes:
- If we match headline price at small volumes we compress unit economics significantly; prefer structuring via tiers/credits and PS value-adds.
- Need Karthik to confirm whether we can offer any temporary higher concurrency guarantees for onboarding without violating capacity commitments.

I’ll draft a single-page summary and the PDF of proposed terms for Sean to send.

—Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference', 'From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: Sara Hunter <sara.hunter@hearthline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@hearthline.com
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposed commercial response to Streamline offer

Sara — thanks again for sending the Streamline term sheet. We reviewed internally and put together a concise counter that balances your economic ask with a predictable operational path. High level:

- Offer: 12-month committed agreement with tiered discounts (attached PDF: Redwood_proposed_terms_v1.pdf)
  - Tiers: 0–5B tokens: $0.0012/token
  - 5–20B tokens: $0.00102/token (-15%)
  - 20B+ tokens: $0.000936/token (-22% at scale)
- $50,000 onboarding credit (applied against first invoice)
- 60 engineer-hours of migration assistance (applied across onboarding)
- SLA: 99.9% availability, with a 30-day rollback clause if perf regressions occur during cutover

Next steps:
1) Please confirm procurement contact and target decision date.
2) If the economics look viable, we’ll generate a tailored Master Services Agreement and a DocuSign packet for signature.

I’ve attached the one-pager terms for procurement. If you’d like, we can schedule a short call Thursday to walk procurement through the differences versus Streamline.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Redwood_proposed_terms_v1.pdf (application/pdf)', 'From: Sara Hunter <sara.hunter@hearthline.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@hearthline.com
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed commercial response to Streamline offer

Thanks, Sean — that all looks reasonable. Procurement will review the PDF and compare against the Streamline docs; I’ve looped procurement (procurement@hearthline.com) for their intake. They’ve asked for a short table comparing cash impact over 12 months (we’ll need the expected monthly burn numbers from you) — can you drop those figures into the HubSpot record? HubSpot ID is included below.

We have a procurement call scheduled for Friday at 10am PT — we’ll plan to discuss your terms then. I’ve also reattached the Streamline term sheet for reference (they want us to keep the onboarding credit in the negotiation).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sara Hunter
Head of Platform Engineering
Hearthline Analytics

---
Attachment: Streamline_offer_v2.pdf (application/pdf)']
